purpose: Documented, reviewed drift of R-169 frozen configuration after R-169 closed (done). A freeze guards reproducibility of the frozen runs; it does not forbid evolving the product forever. Every entry: which file moved, frozen vs current short sha256, why, and the consequence. The runners' check_freeze is NOT relaxed: v2-v5 runners refuse any new held-out run on drift. Tests accept drift only when it matches this ledger exactly; any further change needs a new entry.

entries.change: R-170 batch 10: code_generator returns tool_output.code on the supplied-code path (was metadata only) and no longer cuts LLM code at 8000 chars (bounded at 64000, omitted above with size+sha256).
entries.consequence: All R-169 results (v1-v5, b1-b3, and b4s which runs on its own pre-change commit) stay attributable to the frozen code; new held-out runs of v2-v5 are refused by check_freeze. The v5 code_generator path used by the code tasks now returns the full code text (its answer and ok are unchanged).

entries.change: R-170 batch 12: strategist/architect/designer/reviewer return ok=False (task_not_completed) when core/task_fit finds no evidence the requested task was done; reviewer gains structured findings and checks (empty-input division/index, SQL built by formatting, eval/exec, == True/False, range(len())); strategist parses objectives listed in the request.
entries.consequence: The v2-v5 baseline uses only the code_generator path of real_dispatcher; the four changed handlers are not on any R-169 path. All R-169 results stay attributable to their recorded commits; new held-out runs of v2-v5 are still refused by check_freeze.

entries.change: R-170 batch 16 (lang-retry candidate): the keyless branch routes through _keyless_maybe_lang_retry — one bounded regeneration when the reply language mismatches the prompt's detected language (independent detector, contextvar/env gated, default OFF, deterministic: second accepted if ok, first kept on retry error, never a third attempt). Also a consuming get_last_lang_retry() hook for the pilot recorder. Baseline behavior with the policy OFF is unchanged (early return to _keyless_complete).
entries.consequence: All R-169 results (v1-v7, and the v8 arms with the contextvar OFF: v2/v4) stay attributable to the frozen code; new held-out runs of v2-v5 remain refused by check_freeze. The v4r arm (batch 16) runs with the contextvar ON by design — that is the candidate under judgment, recorded in PREREGISTRATION_V8.

entries.change: R-170 batch 16 CI fix (log 317): retry metadata capture sink (begin_lang_retry_capture/end_lang_retry_capture) so lang_retry metadata crosses the Task boundary that asyncio.wait_for creates on Python 3.11 (ContextVar.set inside a child task is invisible to the caller). get_last_lang_retry() reads the sink when one is active, otherwise the previous behavior is unchanged. No change to the retry policy, the detector, the provider call count or the reply.
entries.consequence: Recording only: the policy (default OFF), its decisions and the replies are unchanged, so all R-169/R-170 results incl. the v9 judgment stay attributable to their recorded commits; new held-out runs of v2-v5 remain refused by check_freeze.

entries.change: R-172 batch 2 (D-116): the code-sandbox child is now network-free — an audit hook installed in the sandbox bootstrap before the user code runs blocks every socket.* event (connect, DNS, bind, construction), closing the residual documented in SECURITY.md. run_sandboxed_python's docstring updated to match.
entries.consequence: All R-169 results stay attributable to the frozen code; the runners' check_freeze is NOT relaxed — new held-out runs of v2-v5 are still refused on drift (the ledger documents it, the guard keeps refusing). The sandbox behavior change is covered by tests/test_r172_batch2_security_limits.py (socket and DNS attempts fail closed inside the sandbox).

entries.change: R-175 phase 1 (D-128): a documented 6-line merge at the bottom of _HANDLERS — the core tool library (core/tools_stdlib.py, 80 deterministic hermetic tools) is merged into the executable surface to reach the spec's phase-1 target of 100 tools. The 20 specialist handlers are byte-untouched; tools_stdlib never imports this module (the no-bypass rule holds).
entries.consequence: All R-169 results (v1-v5, b1-b3, b4s) stay attributable to the frozen code; new held-out runs of v2-v5 are refused by check_freeze exactly as before (the ledger chain now leads to this sha). The 20 specialist handler behaviors are unchanged; the 80 new tools are additive dispatch entries (their gate enforcement is the same runtime gate).
